newsitem.title: USA: Fed's Broaddus says U.S. labor market tight.
newsitem.headline: Fed's Broaddus says U.S. labor market tight.

text.p: Richmond Federal Reserve President Alfred Broaddus said the U.S. labor market in many ways was tight "across the board."
But Broaddus also said he has not seen significant bottlenecks forming in the U.S. economy.
Speaking after a reception at Christopher Newport University, Broaddus told reporters, "We have not seen significant bottlnecks today .... that's a very encouraging condition for me."

But Broaddus said, "Labor markets are tight. They are very tight. I don't know that I would describe it as a bottleneck, but some of the information we've got suggests that there is evidence that ... firms are having difficulties finding the kinds of workers they need."
